<a id="PostgresSql"></a>

### PostgreSQL's dialect

`PostgresSql` · `src/sql.ts:59`

How PostgreSQL names the parameters of a statement and types its columns.

Source: PostgreSQL: Value Expressions, Positional Parameters ($n); Numeric Types (double precision); Character Types (text) · `https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-expressions.html#SQL-EXPRESSIONS-PARAMETERS-POSITIONAL`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `parameter` | `$` | Opens a positional parameter: then its position |
| `first` | `1` | The position of the first parameter |
| `text` | `TEXT` | The type of a column of text |
| `number` | `DOUBLE PRECISION` | The type of a column of numbers (an 8-byte floating point number, as SQLite's REAL) |

- Used by: [PostgreSQL's dialect](infra.md#PostgresDialect), [PostgreSQL parameter](#PostgresParameter)

<a id="Sql"></a>

### SQL

`Sql` · `src/sql.ts:14`

The statements the service writes, as SQL defines them and as SQLite and PostgreSQL both read them.

Source: ISO/IEC 9075 (SQL): SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, CREATE TABLE; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, as SQLite and PostgreSQL both accept it · `https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-commands.html`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `space` | `" "` | Separates the words of a statement |
| `comma` | `,` | Separates the items of a list (columns, values, definitions) |
| `open` | `(` | Opens a list of columns, of values or of definitions |
| `close` | `)` | Closes it |
| `equals` | `=` | Compares a column with a value, or gives it one |
| `select` | `SELECT` | Reads columns |
| `from` | `FROM` | Names the table read |
| `where` | `WHERE` | Introduces the condition the rows must meet |
| `insertInto` | `INSERT INTO` | Adds a row to a table |
| `values` | `VALUES` | Introduces the values of the row |
| `update` | `UPDATE` | Changes rows of a table |
| `set` | `SET` | Introduces the columns changed |
| `createTable` | `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` | Creates a table, unless it exists |
| `primaryKey` | `PRIMARY KEY` | The column that identifies a row |
| `notNull` | `NOT NULL` | A column that always has a value |
| `references` | `REFERENCES` | A column whose value is the key of a row of another table |
| `countAll` | `count(*)` | The number of rows |
| `as` | `AS` | Names a result column |

- Maintained by: karim
- Defines: [Column definition](#ColumnDefinition), [Condition on a column](#ColumnEquals), [Count](#CountRows), [Table creation](#CreateTable), [Insertion](#InsertRow), [Selection](#SelectRows), [List](#SqlList), [Update](#UpdateRows)
- Used by: [Column definition](#ColumnDefinition), [Condition on a column](#ColumnEquals), [Count](#CountRows), [Table creation](#CreateTable), [Insertion](#InsertRow), [Selection](#SelectRows), [List](#SqlList), [Update](#UpdateRows)

### SQLite's dialect

`SqliteSql` · `src/sql.ts:44`

How SQLite names the parameters of a statement and types its columns.

Source: SQLite: SQL As Understood By SQLite, Parameters (?); Datatypes In SQLite (TEXT, REAL) · `https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#varparam`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `parameter` | `?` | A parameter: the next value given with the statement |
| `text` | `TEXT` | The type of a column of text |
| `number` | `REAL` | The type of a column of numbers (an 8-byte floating point number) |
